p: One of the best things about skating in Basingstoke is what sits right alongside it. Milestones Museum is also at the Leisure Park, and it's a brilliant contrast to the cold of the rink: a recreated Hampshire high street from the past, complete with old shopfronts, vintage vehicles and the kind of nostalgic detail that has grandparents pointing at things and saying "we had one of those". Pair the two and you've got a full day without moving the car.

Before your session, give everyone a quick pep talk about rink etiquette. Skate in the same direction as everyone else, don't stop dead in the middle of the ice, and if you need a breather, pull over to the side. Little ones should stay close to a grown-up, especially at busy weekend sessions when the confident teenagers are out in force.

A few comfort tips go a long way too. Wear trousers rather than shorts (the ice is wet when you sit on it), bring gloves, and leave chunky jewellery and loose scarves at home. A small bag is easier than a big one, and you'll want to keep pockets zipped so nothing goes skidding across the ice.

If you're making a weekend of it, the Hampshire countryside is close at hand. The Vyne, a National Trust house with lovely grounds, is just north of town, and the Basingstoke Canal towpath makes for an easy, peaceful walk. After all that skating, a bit of gentle countryside is just the ticket.
